faq.q: Can a foreign company establish a wholly owned subsidiary in India?
faq.a: Yes. In most sectors a foreign company can hold 100% of an Indian private limited company under the automatic route, subject to India's FDI policy, sectoral caps and FEMA reporting. We confirm the route that applies to your sector before incorporation.

faq.q: Does GAA provide resident director services?
faq.a: Yes. Every Indian company needs at least one director who is resident in India. We can provide an eligible resident director and support the related board and compliance responsibilities.

faq.q: Can you assist with bank account opening and Razorpay integration?
faq.a: Yes. We coordinate account opening and KYC with Indian banks and support Razorpay merchant onboarding and integration so you can start collecting payments.

faq.q: What are the ongoing compliance requirements after incorporation?
faq.a: Typically board and shareholder meetings, annual MCA filings, statutory registers, GST and TDS returns, income-tax filings, statutory audit and FEMA reporting such as the annual FLA return. We set up a compliance calendar for your entity.

faq.q: Can we engage GAA for only specific services?
faq.a: Yes. You can engage us for a single service, such as incorporation or a resident director, or for a complete market entry and ongoing operations package.

faq.q: Do you advise private companies as well as public companies?
faq.a: Yes. We advise private and public companies, LLPs and their promoters and boards on company law and governance matters.

faq.q: What does a secretarial audit cover?
faq.a: A secretarial audit reviews a company’s compliance with the Companies Act, 2013 and other applicable laws and rules. It is mandatory for certain classes of companies and is a useful health check for others.

faq.q: Can you take care of our annual ROC filings?
faq.a: Yes. We prepare and file the annual return and financial statements with the Registrar of Companies and track event-based filings during the year.

faq.q: Can you help with changes to our share capital or shareholding?
faq.a: Yes. We handle allotments, transfers, increases in authorised capital and the related board and shareholder approvals and filings.

faq.q: Can we engage you for a single matter?
faq.a: Yes. You can engage us for a single opinion or transaction, or on an ongoing retainer.

faq.q: What does legal and secretarial due diligence cover?
faq.a: It reviews a company’s incorporation documents, statutory registers, filings, approvals, shareholding history and material contracts to identify gaps and risks before a transaction.

faq.q: Do you handle mergers and demergers under the Companies Act?
faq.a: Yes. We support schemes of merger, amalgamation and demerger, including the documentation, approvals and filings involved, working with other advisers where required.

faq.q: Can you help with transactions involving foreign investors?
faq.a: Yes. We advise on FEMA aspects such as pricing guidelines and reporting for share transfers and investments involving non-residents.

faq.q: Do you prepare the transaction documents?
faq.a: Yes. We prepare and review term sheets, share purchase and shareholders’ agreements and the resolutions needed to complete the transaction.

faq.q: Can we engage you only for due diligence?

faq.q: When should we start preparing for a fundraise?
faq.a: Ideally before you approach investors. A readiness review of your records, filings and cap table helps due diligence go smoothly and avoids delays at closing.

faq.q: Do you help with term sheets and shareholders’ agreements?
faq.a: Yes. We review term sheets and draft or review share subscription and shareholders’ agreements, working with you through negotiation.

faq.q: What filings are needed after shares are allotted?
faq.a: Allotments need board and, where applicable, shareholder approvals, the return of allotment and related filings with the Registrar of Companies, and updates to statutory registers. Investment from non-residents also needs FEMA reporting.

faq.q: Can you help set up an ESOP scheme?
faq.a: Yes. We help design the scheme, prepare the documents and obtain the approvals needed to put it in place.

faq.q: Do you work with investors as well as companies?
faq.a: Yes. We can support investors with due diligence and documentation for their investments.

faq.q: What net owned fund is needed to register an NBFC?
faq.a: The RBI prescribes a minimum net owned fund for each category of NBFC, and these requirements have been revised under the scale-based regulatory framework. We confirm the current requirement for your proposed category before you apply.

faq.q: How long does NBFC registration take?
faq.a: It depends on the completeness of the application and the RBI’s review. We prepare a complete application and help you respond to any queries to avoid delays.

faq.q: Does a change in shareholding need RBI approval?
faq.a: Prior RBI approval is generally needed for a change in control, for acquisitions of shareholding above the thresholds the RBI specifies, and for certain changes in management. We assess whether approval is needed and handle the application.

faq.q: Which returns does an NBFC need to file with the RBI?
faq.a: This depends on the NBFC’s category, size and activities. We map the returns that apply to you and maintain a filing calendar.

faq.q: Can you act as our ongoing compliance team?
faq.a: Yes. Our NBFC Compliance Office covers RBI reporting, board and governance support and corporate secretarial compliance on a retainer basis.

faq.q: Which entity should we choose for our startup?
faq.a: Most startups that plan to raise external funding incorporate as a private limited company. We help you weigh the options, including an LLP, based on your plans.

faq.q: What are the annual compliance requirements for a private limited company?
faq.a: Typically board meetings, an annual general meeting, filing financial statements and the annual return with the Registrar of Companies and director KYC, along with event-based filings during the year.

faq.q: Can you help us get Startup India recognition?
faq.a: Yes. We assess eligibility and prepare the application for DPIIT recognition under the Startup India initiative.

faq.q: Can founders based outside India start a company here?
faq.a: Yes, subject to FEMA and FDI rules. Every Indian company needs at least one director who is resident in India, and we can help with this.

faq.q: Do you support startups after they raise funding?
faq.a: Yes. We handle allotment and FEMA filings for the round and continue with ongoing compliance, ESOPs and investor reporting.
